unmapped: Losses ell_{t,u} in [-1,1] with E[ell_{t,u}] = <u, ell_t> for arbitrary ell_t in R^d
settings.definition_quote: In all settings but MDPs, we assume $\ell_{t,u}\in[-1,1]$. In the adversarial regime, $(\ell_{t,u})_{u\in\calX}$ is generated arbitrarily subject to the structure of the concrete setting (e.g., in linear bandits, $\E[\ell_{t,u}]=\inner{u,\ell_t}$ for arbitrary $\ell_t\in\mathbb{R}^d$).

unmapped: Uniform gap: E[ell_{t,x}-ell_{t,x*}] >= Delta - C_t for all x != x*, with C = sum_t C_t
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic regime, we further assume that there exists an action $x^\star\in\calX$ and a gap $\Delta>0$ such that $\E[\ell_{t,x}-\ell_{t,x^\star}]\geq \Delta$ for all $x\neq x^\star$. We also consider the corrupted stochastic regime, where the assumption is relaxed to $\E[\ell_{t,x}-\ell_{t,x^\star}]\geq \Delta-C_t$ for some $C_t\geq 0$. We define $C=\sum_{t=1}^T C_t$.

source.label: thm: VR scrible
source.quote:
In the ``learning with predictions'' setting, \pref{alg: VR scrible} achieves a second-order regret bound of $O\Big(d\sqrt{
u \log(T)\sum_{t=1}^T (\ell_{t,A_t}-m_{t,A_t})^2} + d
u\log T\Big)$ in the adversarial regime, where $d$ is the feature dimension, $
u\leq d$ is the self-concordance parameter of the regularizer

results.notes: Second-order (data-dependent) bound; nu mapped to vartheta. Action set is finite X with conv(X) used by the algorithm.

source.label: thm: VR scrible
source.quote: This also implies a first-order regret bound of $O\Big(d\sqrt{\nu\log (T)\sum_{t=1}^T \ell_{t,u}}\Big)$ if $\ell_{t,x}\geq 0$ and $m_t=\mathbf{0}$

results.notes: First-order bound; proof includes an additive d*nu*log T term omitted in the statement. L_star is the comparator's cumulative loss.

conditions: unique optimal action x* with uniform gap Delta (up to corruption)
